At u=400 the critical x³B_u is −0.0500000611 for c=1, κ=1/2 and −0.2500027902 for c=2, κ=7/8, against −0.05 and −0.25. Off-critical and untwisted checks corroborate the leading terms.
correctness.rationale: The tail at integer threshold is S(x)=1−[1−(c/x)^p]^κ, x=u+c, and conditioning on Y≥u gives the numerator ∑_{j≥1}S(x+j), not a sum starting at zero. Since S(x) is asymptotic to κc^p x^(−p), finiteness is exactly p>1. The fixed-parameter Taylor remainder is summable uniformly over x+j≥x; upon normalization the remainder through the third survival term is O(x^(1−3p)). Euler–Maclaurin for x^s ζ(s,x+1) gives x/(s−1)−1/2+s/(12x)−s(s+1)(s+2)/(720x³)+O(x^(−5)). The common −1/2 cancels from carrier differences. At p=2, write a=c², d=(κ−1)/2 and e=(κ−1)(κ−2)/6. Then C1=1/6+2da/3 and C3=−1/30−da/6+a²[(2/3)d²−(4/5)e]; the next error is O(x^(−5)). The unique admissible zero of C1 requires a>1/2 and yields C3=(1−4a)/60<0, including −1/20 at a=1. The lattice/carrier ordering off p=2 and the exact κ=1 baseline follow by order comparison, and structural zero inflation cancels at positive thresholds.
residual_risks: Finite numerical diagnostics do not establish eventual signs or asymptotic remainders. The proof is pointwise in fixed parameters and does not give a uniform boundary-layer approximation when parameters vary with threshold.

value.rationale: A mean-excess plot for a tail model depends on the direction and size of the systematic population bias. The result delineates whether discretization or the carrier controls that bias, and resolves the sign and exact changed order on their cancellation boundary. That boundary information is useful even without a uniform or sampling-theoretic extension.
residual_risks: No calibration of estimator uncertainty or inference at a drifting critical parameter is supplied.
